findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify a cross-platform subprocess-timeout/kill strategy for the DC renderer (e.g. process-group kill on POSIX, taskkill /T or Job Objects on Windows) so the timeout fallback works on Windows as well as POSIX.
evidence: Plan quote: 'Bound subprocess work per field. Kill the process group on timeout. Fall back without content loss.'
Platform fact: os.killpg and start_new_session/setsid process-group semantics are POSIX-only; on Windows there is no process group to signal, so a killpg-based timeout path is unavailable.
Matrix: rebar must run on Windows platform.
findings.finding: The DC robustness step 'Kill the process group on timeout' assumes POSIX process-group semantics (setsid/os.killpg), which do not exist on Windows.
findings.location: Child responsibilities → DC robustness: 'Kill the process group on timeout.'
scenarios: Windows developer workstation / Windows CI runner: DC render on a pathological body hits the timeout; the process-group kill path raises AttributeError (os.killpg absent) or is a no-op, so the pandoc subprocess is not terminated and the timeout guard fails to bound the work — the user witnesses a hang or a crash instead of the intended identity fallback.
findings.suggested_fix: Describe the timeout termination for both platforms: use start_new_session + os.killpg on POSIX, and a Windows-specific mechanism (CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP + terminate of the process tree, or a Job Object) on Windows, with the identity fallback triggered on either.

evidence: Plan quote: 'Use two asymmetric codecs behind one state-based echo-safety layer on the existing adapters/jira_family/rich_text.py seam.'

Plan quote: 'Echo safety for both targets uses the existing ADR-0026 per-binding baseline' — ADR-0026 is referenced as pre-existing; the new asymmetric-codec/last-write-wins/origin-gating decisions are not tied to an ADR update.

findings.location: Design section: 'Use two asymmetric codecs behind one state-based echo-safety layer'
scenarios: Future maintainer changing the Cloud vs DC codec asymmetry or the last-write-wins conflict policy has no recorded rationale for why DC is one-way while Cloud is bidirectional and why last-write-wins was chosen over reject-on-conflict.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Name pandoc's native `jira` output writer as the DC-path baseline and justify the segmenting/verbatim design against using that writer end-to-end (what loss/failure mode segmentation prevents that the stock writer does not).
evidence: Plan: 'A segmenting renderer converts structurally safe units, substitutes prose arrows before pandoc, wraps ASCII tables in noformat, plus passes dangerous units through verbatim.'
Pandoc natively supports `jira` as an output format (pandoc.org; confirmed via web search) — the presumed underlying mechanism, unnamed in the plan.
Plan does justify segmentation on lossiness ('Jira wiki markup is lossy for punctuation-dense prose'), but does not compare against the whole-body pandoc jira writer as the baseline.
findings.finding: The DC renderer relies on pandoc but never acknowledges pandoc's native `jira` output writer as the prior-art baseline it extends, nor justifies the custom segmenting-renderer + verbatim-passthrough design against simply using pandoc's built-in jira writer end-to-end.
findings.location: Design / Child responsibilities: DC renderer capability (wiki_render.py)
scenarios: Reviewer/maintainer cannot tell whether the segmenting complexity is warranted vs pandoc's stock jira writer
Future contributor re-derives the loss analysis pandoc's writer already encodes
findings.suggested_fix: In the DC renderer capability section, state that the renderer wraps pandoc's `-t jira` writer and enumerate the specific structures where the stock writer loses/corrupts content (punctuation-dense prose, ASCII tables), justifying the per-unit segmentation and verbatim passthrough as the mitigation.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Assign inbound-differ DC codec-aware echo-suppression (Jira wiki echo decodes/normalizes to the local Markdown) to a named child's acceptance criteria so parent AC15 is covered offline, not only by the live 3289 assertion.
evidence: Parent Design: 'Echo safety for both targets uses the existing ADR-0026 per-binding baseline plus normalize_outbound ... Three-way baseline/local/remote comparison'

3388 Design decision 1 pins the two compares to `outbound_field_diff.py` (`:288`, `_suppressed_by_inbound`, `_local_matches_baseline`) and states `_remote_matches_baseline` and inbound description stay UNCHANGED/additive
3388 Scope (OUT): 'no change to ... inbound_fields.normalize_rich_text'
3289 roster AC only pins `normalize_rich_text` back-compat and a live end-to-end echo assertion; it names no inbound-differ codec-aware suppression AC

Parent AC15: 'The second live DC reconcile pass performs no body update' — depends on the inbound differ recognizing the DC wiki echo as unchanged, which no sibling AC delivers as an offline/unit guarantee
findings.finding: G4 dependency-gap / consumer-impact: the parent design states echo safety for BOTH Cloud and DC uses the ADR-0026 baseline plus normalize_outbound three-way compare, but 3388's roster scope covers only the OUTBOUND differ compares (emit + baseline local-side normalization). The INBOUND differ, which the parent's round-trip echo-safety implicitly depends on, is not adjusted by any sibling's stated acceptance criteria: 3388 explicitly leaves inbound description as additive and does not claim an inbound codec-aware echo-suppression AC, and 3289 only claims a live end-to-end echo assertion plus the normalize_rich_text contract test. For the DC rich path, a converged body's Jira-echoed wiki does not decode back to the local Markdown through the Cloud-ADF-only inbound normalizer, so the inbound differ would re-pull the echo every pass — an owned-by-none scope gap relative to parent AC15 (second live DC pass performs no body update) and AC7.
findings.location: child 3388-96e8-e14e-4221 (Scope OUT) and child 3289-7fe4-2fea-4c35 (AC coverage of AC15)
scenarios: DC rich cutover enabled: rebar authors Markdown, pushes rendered wiki; on the next pass the inbound differ normalizes Jira's wiki via the Cloud ADF codec only, sees it != local Markdown, and emits an inbound description update every pass — pulling Jira's echo of rebar's own push back over the local body
AC15 would fail live on the second pass (inbound=1) despite the outbound path being echo-safe
findings.suggested_fix: Add an inbound echo-suppression AC to 3388 (or a named owner) mirroring the outbound `_baseline_form_matches` / `normalize_outbound` compare on the inbound differ for the description field, with an offline test proving a canonicalizing DC echo yields inbound=0 across passes; keep 3289 as the live confirmation.
